# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**From:** Taylor Foster
Member ID: W684120124
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-23 — Reference number POC-157F6EFE74-80557**
**Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0743 – Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the lower back decompression surgery (CPT 63030) that my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, requested for me. The notice dated 2026-08-23 states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the criteria published in Aetna's own policy, CPB 0743 – Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion, match what is already documented in my medical records.

Below I have set out the plan's published criteria in its own words, followed by what my records show.

## 1. Conservative therapy

The plan's policy states:

> "Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy Footnote1 * (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management, noted below); and"

and:

> "Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression."

My records establish this. I completed supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 14 weeks from 2026-04-03 to 2026-07-10, with 24 visits completed. That is well beyond the six weeks the policy requires, and all of it occurred within the past year. I also took NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief, and I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19 that gave me only about three weeks of partial relief. My symptoms have continued for 12 months and have been getting worse, not better.

## 2. Documentation of the physical therapy

The plan's policy states:

> "The member should participate in physical therapy for the entire required duration of conservative management (six weeks or three months, depending upon the indication for surgery). Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

My records establish this. My physical therapy is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, which records the full course of 24 visits from 2026-04-03 to 2026-07-10. If that note was not included in the material the reviewer saw, I am asking that it be requested and reviewed before a decision is made.

## 3. Signs or symptoms of neural compression

The plan's policy states:

> "Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and"

My records establish this. I have radicular pain going down into my right calf. My examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level — the same level my surgeon proposes to treat.

## 4. Advanced imaging findings

The plan's policy states:

> "Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and"

My records establish this. My MRI of the lumbar spine, performed on 2026-07-15, reports an L4-L5 disc extrusion with **severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root**. That is severe stenosis — not mild or mild to moderate — and it is nerve root compression, and it is on the right side, which is the side my pain and deficit are on.

## 5. Timing of the imaging

The plan's policy states:

> "Advanced imaging studies are required prior to any spinal surgery. The imaging should be performed within the past year, or after the onset of the current constellation of symptoms or any relevant surgical procedures, whichever is sooner."

My records establish this. The MRI was performed on 2026-07-15, within the past year and after my symptoms began.

The plan's policy also states:

> "For purposes of this policy, Aetna will consider the official written report of advanced imaging studies (e.g., CT, MRI, myelogram). If the operating surgeon disagrees with the official written report, the surgeon should document that disagreement."

The findings I have quoted above are from the official written MRI report itself, which is the source the policy says Aetna will consider.

## 6. Limitation of my daily activities

The plan's policy states:

> "Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression;"

My records establish this. I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radiating pain into my right calf. My back pain has been progressive over 12 months and is not relieved by rest.

## 7. Examination by the operating surgeon

The plan's policy states:

> "Medical records must document that a physical examination, including a neurologic examination, has been performed by or reviewed by the operating surgeon."

My records establish this. Dr. Marchetti, an orthopedic surgeon, is the operating surgeon, and the examination findings in my chart — positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level — are documented in the prior authorization packet he submitted. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

## 8. Other sources of pain

The plan's policy states:

> "All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning; and"

My records establish this. The MRI report identifies the pathology at L4-L5 — the level for which surgery is requested — and my clinical findings correspond to that same level. My records do not describe pathology at any other level that would be left out of the surgical plan.

---

## What I am asking for

I want to be straightforward about two things. First, the denial notice I received told me only that the request "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." It did not tell me which specific criterion in CPB 0743 Aetna found unmet. Second, some of the provisions in the policy I was given introduce further lists of conditions that were not reproduced for me, so there may be additional requirements I have not been able to address here. If Aetna is relying on one of those, I ask that the plan identify the specific criterion it applied so that I have a fair chance to respond to it with the relevant records.

For the criteria I can see, my records line up with each one: more than six weeks of recent, in-person, supervised physical therapy plus medication and an injection trial; documented radicular symptoms and a corresponding neurologic deficit; a severe lateral recess stenosis with nerve root compression on an MRI performed within the past year at the level that matches my symptoms; clear limitation of my daily activities; and an examination performed by my operating surgeon.

I respectfully ask Aetna to overturn the denial of reference number POC-157F6EFE74-80557 and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Marchetti. Please also send me a copy of the specific clinical criteria and the reviewer's rationale used in this determination.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-02-19**, within 180 days of the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals), sent by fax to **859-425-3379** or mailed to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I can also be reached at 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my member card if any additional information is needed.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I am enclosing the records referenced above.

**Enclosures:**
- Physical therapy discharge note (24 visits, 2026-04-03 to 2026-07-10)
- MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-07-15
- Office/operative planning notes from Dr. Marchetti
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-23
- [Any other documents I am including]

Sincerely,

**Taylor Foster**
Member ID: W684120124
Reference number: POC-157F6EFE74-80557
[Signature]
[Date]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
